# Interview Experience - 191 - Amazon | Software Development Engineer | SDE II (L5)

Team Roundz

Share

### Summary

Job Role: Software Development Engineer

Number of Rounds: 5

Offer Status: Rejected

Location: Canada

Candidate Name: Not disclosing due to signed NDA

---

## Interview Process

I was reached out to by a recruiter via LinkedIn. The process for the Amazon SDE II role in Canada consisted of one Online Assessment followed by a Virtual Onsite with four rounds.

The Online Assessment had two coding questions and a few work-simulation style questions based on Amazon’s Leadership Principles.

The Virtual Onsite had four rounds spread over a single day, with a strong focus on both technical problem-solving and Leadership Principles. Each round lasted about an hour. Two weeks after the interview, my recruiter informed me of the rejection. No feedback was shared, except that I could reapply after one year.

---

## Preparation Guide

Despite having 12 years of industry experience, the preparation turned out to be a key factor. The main challenge was recalling solutions to familiar problems under time pressure. My preparation approach was:

Practiced LeetCode medium and hard questions, though not extensively enough.

Reviewed common system design problems, including real-world applications.

Prepared for Leadership Principles by reflecting on professional experiences.

Underestimated Binary Tree and game-style coding problems, which later showed up in the interviews.

Looking back, I should have practiced more coding under timed conditions, especially in areas I had not touched in a while like trees and grid-based games.

---

## Interview Rounds

---

### Round 1: Online Assessment

Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty Level: Medium

Experience:The Online Assessment contained two coding questions and several Leadership Principle-based situational questions.

Question 1: Packets and Channels problem (similar to this discussion). I solved it perfectly.

Question 2: A LeetCode Medium problem (I don’t remember the exact one). I wrote a brute force solution that only passed about 50% of test cases.

Leadership Principles questions simulating real workplace decisions.

Key Learnings:Even if a problem looks familiar, not remembering the approach can be costly. Review and rehearse problem-solving strategies repeatedly. Expect behavioral/LP-based simulations even in the OA.

---

### Round 2: Virtual Onsite – Round 1

Duration: 60 minutes

Difficulty Level: Difficult

Experience:This round combined Leadership Principles with a Binary Tree coding problem.

Coding Problem: Return the list of nodes within an S distance from a given target node in a Binary Tree.

I struggled here and needed hints from the interviewer. Eventually, I was able to piece together a solution with some help.

Key Learnings:Binary Tree problems come up often at Amazon interviews. It’s important to practice them thoroughly. When stuck, stay receptive to interviewer guidance and build incrementally.

---

### Round 3: Virtual Onsite – Round 2

Duration: 60 minutes

Difficulty Level: Medium

Experience:Leadership Principles questions came first, followed by a coding problem:

Coding Problem: Given a set of meetings, check if a person can attend all of them.

Example:`[[10,30],[20,50]] → False`

Example:`[[0,15],[20,40],[60,100]] → True`

I solved this problem perfectly within the time.

Key Learnings:Interval-based scheduling and meeting problems are standard. Practicing them pays off directly.

---

### Round 4: Virtual Onsite – Round 3

Duration: 60 minutes

Difficulty Level: Medium

Experience:This round was with the Hiring Manager and focused on Leadership Principles and System Design.

System Design Problem: Design a food delivery app like Uber.

I was able to provide a strong design and discuss multiple follow-up questions, including scalability and real-world considerations.

Key Learnings:At the SDE II level, expect system design questions modeled on widely used applications. Be ready not just to design but also to handle iterative follow-up discussions.

---

### Round 5: Virtual Onsite – Round 4

Duration: 60 minutes

Difficulty Level: Medium

Experience:Leadership Principles questions were followed by a coding exercise:

Coding Problem: Design and implement a simple Tic Tac Toe game (3x3 matrix, 2 players).

I started strong, but towards the end, I became confused while handling winner/tie conditions. Fatigue was a factor since this was the last of four back-to-back interviews.

Key Learnings:Game-based logic problems may look simple but can trip you up under pressure. Long interview days are mentally exhausting—find strategies to stay fresh and alert until the end.

---

## Final Thoughts

The Amazon interview process is thorough and balances technical problem-solving with Leadership Principles evaluation. Some final takeaways:

Leadership Principles are as important as coding and system design—practice articulating your experiences clearly.

Even with extensive work experience, it’s crucial to brush up on fundamental coding areas like Binary Trees, intervals, and simple board games.

Stamina matters. Four back-to-back technical rounds are draining, and mental fatigue can affect performance.

Always revisit problems you’ve solved in the past. Forgetting the approach under pressure can be the difference between success and failure.

Despite the rejection, the experience highlighted clear areas for improvement. I’ll focus more on Binary Trees, system design practice, and endurance for long interview days before reapplying.
